newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S ASC SAYS PAUL MORGAN AGREES DEMANDS.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S ASC SAYS PAUL MORGAN AGREES DEMANDS.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Thursday that Brisbane broker Paul Morgan Securities had agreed to various demands after an investigation into a capital raising in 1996.

The ASC said the broker had given undertakings to compensate investors and implement strict internal compliance reviews following an investigation by the ASC into a capital raising without a prospectus for Minyango Resources NL in late 1996.
Minyango is an unlisted mining company and is currently subject to a deed of company arrangement.

The ASC said Paul Morgan Securities had undertaken to compensate clients adversely affected by its conduct by offering to buy back their Minyango shares for the full issue price and pay all stamp duty on the transactions.
The investors would not be liable for any commissions.
The ASC said the broker had advised that it no longer employed certain staff involved in the transaction and major internal procedural and management changes had been made.

An independent external consultant has been appointed to review and report on internal legal and regulatory compliance processes at Paul Morgan Securities, a copy of which report would be provided to the ASC, it said.
The ASC said its enquiries into the conduct of former employees was continuing.
